description: Same trust-tiered relation-forming exercise run earlier through ClaudeAdapter (see 2026-09-26_relation_depends_on_pending_review.json) and GrokAdapter (see 2026-09-26_grok_relation_depends_on_pending_review.json), now through GPTAdapter. Seeds the identical claim about project()'s hinge-vs-decoration handling, then asks the model to propose a genuinely connected follow-up and link it via the candidate "relation" field.

seed_claim.content: The kernel project() function treats DEPENDS_ON and CONTRADICTS relations as must-keep structural hinges that are pulled into the workspace unconditionally, while ABOUT relations are treated as optional decoration that only gets filled in if the node budget allows, biased by traversal_weight.
seed_claim.falsification_test: Read project() and confirm DEPENDS_ON/CONTRADICTS are added to must unconditionally while ABOUT is only added to optional.

setup.task: Given the seeded claim about project() treating DEPENDS_ON/CONTRADICTS as must-keep hinges and ABOUT as optional decoration, propose ONE follow-up structural contribution that logically builds on it -- not a fresh, unrelated observation. Use the relation field described in your instructions to actually link your new claim to the seeded one with the relation_type that honestly describes how they connect.

admitted_claim.content: project() first computes the transitive hinge-closure: all nodes reachable from the seed set via only DEPENDS_ON/CONTRADICTS edges, and treats that set as a hard, non-prunable floor. ABOUT traversal occurs only after this closure is fully included. If the hinge-closure alone exceeds the node budget, project() returns an overbudget outcome rather than dropping or truncating any hinge path.
admitted_claim.falsification_test: Create a graph with S DEPENDS_ON B, B DEPENDS_ON C, and an ABOUT node D with high traversal_weight. Seed S. Case 1: node_budget=2. Expected: project() reports overbudget and does not return a projection that omits B or C; observing a projection that includes S but drops B or C (or includes D instead) falsifies the claim. Case 2: node_budget=3 with the same seed: Expected: the result includes {S,B,C} before considering D, regardless of D's traversal_weight; observing D included while any of {S,B,C} is missing falsifies the claim.

relation_proposals_after_run.rationale: Treating DEPENDS_ON/CONTRADICTS as unconditional hinges implies project() must preserve their transitive closure before optional ABOUT fill; without that must-keep premise, enforcing hinge-closure as a hard floor would not be required.

notes: Matches both Claude and Grok on the identical relation-forming task: all three models identified a genuine logical dependency and self-reported DEPENDS_ON accordingly, correctly routed to relation_proposals as PENDING rather than written into relations directly. GPT's follow-up claim is the most rigorously specified of the three, with a two-case falsification_test spelling out exact graph topology and expected/falsifying observations -- notably more thorough than Claude's or Grok's falsification_test for the equivalent fixture, though also by far the slowest (24.9s vs ~8-11s for the others) and most token-hungry (1965 output tokens vs low hundreds/low thousands).
